name: Push Jerk
description: The push jerk is a jerk variation in which the athlete catches the bar in a partial squat with both feet on the same line, as opposed to the split jerk's forward-and-back split stance. The dip-drive mechanics are identical to the split jerk but the catch requires the athlete to drop straight down rather than splitting. It is a useful accessory movement for overhead stability development and is often used as a teaching drill for the split jerk.

execution.starting_position: Bar in front rack position on shoulders. Feet hip-width apart, torso vertical.
execution.setup_instructions: Same starting position as the split jerk. Taken from a clean or the rack.
steps: Step 1: Stand with the bar in the front rack, torso upright.
Step 2: Dip straight down — small controlled knee bend with vertical torso.
Step 3: Drive upward explosively, pressing the bar off the shoulders.
Step 4: Drop the hips straight down to catch the bar overhead in a partial squat, locking the elbows.
Step 5: Stand to full extension while maintaining the locked overhead position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace before the dip. Exhale after standing from the catch.
common_mistakes: Pressing the bar with the arms before full hip extension
Letting the torso lean forward during the dip
safety_considerations: Requires shoulder mobility to achieve a stable overhead position with the bar slightly behind the ears.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead lockout with elbows extended. Catch in a stable partial squat, feet flat.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Explosive drive, fast catch, controlled stand.
coaching_cues: Drive up — then drop straight down
Lock out the elbows fast in the catch
